problem:
What is the standard deviation of the following data set?

$$
7,\,3,\,3,\,5,\,1,\,0,\,2
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Standard Deviation of a Data Set
examples.problem:
What is the standard deviation of the following data set?

$$
7, \: 5, \: 0, \: 2, \: 1, \: 3
$$
examples.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a data set $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$ is the square root of the variance:

$$
\sigma = \sqrt{ \sigma^2 } = \sqrt{ \dfrac{1}{n} \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2 } = \sqrt{ \,\,\, \vphantom{\sum\limits_{i=1}^n} \overline{x^2} - \left( \overline{x} \right)^2 }
$$

First, let's compute $\overline{x}.$ There are $n=6$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot (7+5+0+2+1+3) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot 18 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overline{x^2}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot ({7}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot (49+25+0+4+1+9) \\  & =\frac{88}{6} \\  & =\frac{44}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{44}{3}-{(3)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{44}{3}-9 \\  & =\frac{44-27}{3} \\  & =\frac{17}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the standard deviation is

$$
\sigma = \sqrt{ \sigma^2 } = \sqrt{ \dfrac{17}{3} }.
$$

feedback.problem:
What is the variance of the following data set?

$$
-5,\,-1,\,0,\,-8,\,7,\,0,\,9,\,6
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance can be computed as

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=8$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot (-5-1+0-8+7+0+9+6) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot 8 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot [(-5)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-8)^{2}+{7}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{9}^{2}+{6}^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot [25+1+0+64+49+0+81+36] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot 256 \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =32-{(1)}^{2} \\  & =32-1 \\  & =31.\end{aligned}
$$
